points.description: Names and describes one distinct challenge of mobile routing compared with fixed/wired routing, e.g. adaptation to dynamic topology (nodes joining/leaving or moving unpredictably), security (easy interception or injection of packets over wireless), medium access control (hidden/exposed terminals, near-far effect), QoS, scalability, heterogeneity, dependability, or power consumption. The description must explain why it is a problem in the mobile/wireless setting. Equivalent wording is accepted.

Names and describes a second challenge that is different from the first, using the same standard as P1 (name plus a correct explanation of why it arises in mobile routing). Two variants of the same idea, such as hidden and exposed terminal under one medium-access heading, count as one challenge only.

rubric.notes: Full marks (1) need two different named challenges, each with a correct explanation of why it arises in mobile or wireless routing. Award 0.5 for each correctly named and described distinct challenge. Award 0 for a challenge that is only named, is not specific to mobile/wireless networks, or is wrong. Any challenge from the model answer list is acceptable.
